key_insight: Superfluid helium-4 near a wall still follows a logarithmic law-of-the-wall, but with a strongly reduced, temperature-insensitive effective Kármán constant that signals nonclassical two-fluid behavior.
engineering_relevance: This provides a new wall-flow model for cryogenic He II transport, relevant to designing and operating cooling systems where near-wall shear and pressure losses matter.
method: Measured near-wall velocity in mechanically driven He II pipe flow using molecular tagging velocimetry.
Computed wall shear stress independently from pressure-drop measurements.
Compared profiles across Reynolds numbers up to 1.26×10^6 and multiple temperatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports robust logarithmic velocity profiles in the normal fluid and an effective Kármán constant that stays nearly unchanged across the temperature range studied.
watch_item: The reported wall law is derived for the normal-fluid component in He II pipe flow, so its applicability to other geometries, forcing conditions, or cryogenic operating regimes should be validated before broad use.
paper_title: A nonclassical law of the wall in superfluid helium-4
